text:
micah: Heads-up — found a confusing exit-code behavior in the eval harness CLI when running locally. CI relies on non-zero for validation failures but local `--dry-run` is returning 0.

micah: Repro (on my laptop):
```
$ ./harness local run --config tests/edge-cases.yaml --validate --dry-run
VALIDATION: 3 warnings, 1 error
Summary: FAIL
Exit code: 0
```

micah: Expected exit != 0. Either the `--dry-run` path is swallowing the result or `--validate` isn't propagating. :thinking:

olivia: ugh. that will silently pass CI -> prod checks. thanks for catching. did you run with `--no-cache`? sometimes local cache masks failures.

micah: tried `--no-cache` and also `HARNESs_LOCAL=true` — same output. No extra stack traces.

priya: likely the runner wraps errors and returns 0 on any `--dry-run` because it prints a summary but then returns 0 for UX. we changed that last quarter for local dev convenience. but agree CI needs strictness.

sam: @priya do you remember the PR? iirc there was chatter about making dry-run non-fatal so you can iterate faster. we need opt-in for relaxed mode, not the default.

priya: yep that was #1256. the intent was to avoid failing when people use `--watch` flows. but we didn't gate it behind `--watch`. my bad.

micah: quick proposal: 1) `--dry-run` should preserve validation exit semantics unless `--relax` is passed. 2) add `--exit-on-validate` flag. 3) add unit test in CI for `--validate --dry-run` to assert non-zero on failure.

jonah: sounds good. small change. we should also update docs: CLI page currently says "dry-run simulates runs" but not how it handles exit codes. link: https://redwood.dev/devex/eval-harness/cli#dry-run

sam: +1 on tests. i'll add an integration test that runs a tiny failing config in CI runner job. could we also add a lint check that catches accidental PRs that flip default behavior?

priya: i'll open a quick PR to revert the default behavior and add the `--relax` flag. drafting now. will include a changelog note.

micah: thanks. for immediate relief, is there a way to make our CI job treat the printed "Summary: FAIL" text as a signal? we could `grep` for FAIL but feels fragile.

olivia: avoid fragile greps. better to rely on exit codes. we should also add a post-run step in the harness that writes a machine-readable JSON results file with `status` and `errors` so CI can parse it.

jonah: Agreed. That JSON output is useful for dashboards too. small schema: { "status": "ok|fail", "fail_count": N, "errors": [...] }. The console summary can remain human-friendly.

micah: perfect. Priya, want me to review the PR? I can also add the CI job test.

priya: please! i'll tag you when it's up. planning to include the `--exit-on-validate` option and update the README snippet and the man page.

eval-bot: Note: new issue created by priya -> infra/evalharness#3421: "restore validation exit semantics; add --relax flag; add results JSON"

sam: tiny follow-up: let's add a short entry in the changelog and a one-line deprecation note in the docs for the older behavior so support isn't surprised.

micah: ok i'll draft the CI test now and put it behind a flaky guard so it doesn't block other work until PR merges. will paste commands in thread.

olivia: thanks team. feels low-risk but important for onboarding models — we cannot have silent validation regressions when people bring up quantized variants. :thumbsup:
